bullets.title: Advanced Assessment & Clinical Prioritisation
bullets.text: Patients with complex conditions may show several abnormal findings at the same time. Advanced nursing assessment focuses on identifying the problem that threatens life or function first, while continuing to collect information about the whole clinical picture. Rapid assessment should be followed by focused…

bullets.title: Cardiovascular & Respiratory Emergencies
bullets.text: Acute coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, severe asthma, acute pulmonary oedema and respiratory failure can deteriorate rapidly. Nursing care focuses on early recognition, oxygenation, circulation, monitoring and timely escalation.

bullets.title: Neurological, Renal & Endocrine Emergencies
bullets.text: Neurological, renal and endocrine emergencies can produce rapid changes in consciousness, circulation and electrolyte balance. Nurses need to recognise red flags, protect the patient from immediate harm and support targeted treatment.

bullets.title: Sepsis, Shock & Multisystem Deterioration
bullets.text: Sepsis and shock can progress to multiorgan failure. Early recognition and rapid treatment improve outcomes. Nurses are often the first to recognise the combination of infection, altered perfusion and organ dysfunction.
